content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a [product_name] [article_no]. After powering off the device, I insert a 16GB SD card (formatted with FAT32, not using Quick Format). Next, I power it on, stop the program, navigate to card settings, and select 'load project to card.' Then, I connect by Ethernet and try uploading via [product_name] [version_no]. Both the software and hardware work fine until I attempt the upload; IP addresses are set correctly. I receive an error: 'Upload Failed! There is no such path in SD Card.' During upload, it creates a program name, but the program on the device has no name. I thought that might be the issue, but matching names on both ends didn't resolve it. Is there something I’m missing? Programming through the device’s front buttons is inconvenient, especially with complex projects. I need a quick solution for failures, so off-shift operators can keep things running smoothly. Any guidance on what I should do? I’ve also tried accessing the SD card by connecting it directly to a computer. I see .dat and .bin files, but haven’t found them useful. Thank you, [user_name]
I’m not quite sure what process you’re following. Which type of project are you referring to? Is it [product_name] or [product_name]?
This process is done using the buttons on the front of the [product_name] device to save the project onto the SD card.

You haven’t answered my initial questions. 1) You don’t need to transfer a [product_name] program to the SD card because the device has internal memory for storing programs. 2) You can transfer a [product_name] project from the software to the SD card while the SD card is in the device.
So, I can't use the SD card and device buttons to load the project to the SD card as shown in online videos? Regarding transferring: Is it possible to upload the project, which is what I want to do?
Do you know the differences between a [product_name] program and a [product_name] project?

It’s possible this is where I’m getting confused. I programmed the [product_name] via the front panel and want the ability to program from my computer in the future, for easier updates and device replacements. Right now, the program only lives on the device, and I want to upload it so I can easily restore or modify it later if required.

I’m sorry, but I’m having trouble following your workflow. How does your program created via the device buttons relate to [product_name]? If you want to save a program from the device to your PC, you need to download it using [product_name].

My goal is to save this project like all other PLC projects, ready to load onto replacement hardware. Currently, the project exists only on the device. If it fails, I can’t transfer the program to a new device. So, I need to download it to my computer using [product_name]. What exactly is [product_name]? Does this mean I need different software from what I’m using? I had a feeling I was missing something.
Sorry, I’m unable to assist further. I’m having difficulty understanding your requirements—language might be a barrier.
Is [product_name] available to download? I’m not having any luck finding it with my current searches.
I need to get the [product_name] program using [product_name]. How can I obtain [product_name]?
[product_name] refers to [document], which is the programming software for a [product_name] device.

Hi, there are two options from my perspective: 1. If you program the [product_name] via manual input on the device, the program can't be very large and advanced features are limited. 2. Alternatively, use [document] on your PC. The programming software offers more functions. [document] isn’t free; you pay for it once and can upgrade for free. The current version is [version_no]. Manual programming (option 1) offers little support. For the SD card: If you’ve saved the program from the device onto the SD card and plugged it into your PC, you should find a file called [product_name]_U_P.bin in the root folder. This is a copy of your program. Only a [product_name] device or [document] software can read it; other tools can’t. So even if you managed to copy it, without [document] your PC or another [product_name] device can’t use the SD card’s files.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face confusion when trying to back up and transfer programs created via the device’s front panel to new devices using an SD card and software tools. The main challenge is understanding the correct workflow for exporting locally made programs so that they can be restored to replacement hardware. The error involving a missing path on the SD card, alongside unclear guidance on compatible software and file formats, increases frustration and complicates the process.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect programs developed on the device to be easily exported, backed up, and restored to other devices or computers, similar to the backup workflow they use for other PLC systems.
